title: Intensive and extensive properties
objectives: Classify intensive and extensive properties; apply the split/combine test; use density and mass consistently.
difficulty: Beginner through application; final question is a challenge
instructions: Show reasoning and units. Use a calculator when useful. For conversions use 273.15 and 4.184 J/cal. Numeric checking alone cannot award reasoning points.

questions.prompt: Classify mass and temperature as extensive or intensive.
Classify volume and density for uniform samples at the same state.
Two identical 30 °C portions are combined without energy loss or phase change. Choose the final temperature: A. 15 °C B. 30 °C C. 60 °C. Explain.
A homogeneous 90 g sample is divided into three equal portions with no state change. What is each mass? What happens to its density?
A liquid sample has mass 63 g and volume 70 mL. Calculate its density.
Double the sample in Q05 using an identical portion. Give the new mass, volume and density.
A student argues pressure is extensive because it can change when a gas is compressed. Explain the mistake.

Challenge: Under a stated consistent energy reference, one uniform portion has U=600 J, mass 20 g and temperature 28 °C. Combine three identical portions without other effects. Give total U, total mass and temperature.
